openings.text: At Ada’s tiny bakery stall, Pip pinned a paper label to the cinnamon button with a proud little pat. Nia lifted her bright jam jar. “A fair exchange?” she asked. Ada hoped her baking would make Nia smile, but the label made a very different promise.

At Ada’s tiny bakery stall, Pip pinned “cinnamon” to the button and puffed out his squirrel chest. Nia offered her bright jam jar, while Ada imagined everyone sharing one delicious bite. The little pastry sat between them like a button-sized invitation.

Pip pinned “cinnamon” to Ada’s button, even though this batch had a peppery secret. Nia arrived with berry jam and a hungry grin. “If it’s truly daring,” said Ada, “we can taste it bravely.” Pip’s whiskers trembled with pride.

endings.text: Nia carried the cinnamon button away, berry shine still bright on her fingers. Ada’s stall smelled sweet, while Pip wore the paper label like a tiny sash. It kept slipping sideways, but Pip marched proudly beneath it.
The traded button vanished into Nia’s happy bite, leaving Ada with the jam jar and Pip with a very important paper sash. He paraded past the flour tin, calling, “A fair trade for a splendid snack!”

The pepper-and-berry button disappeared, and three jammy pawprints circled the empty plate. Nia declared it astonishing. Pip bowed to the label, which suddenly looked less like a question and more like a tiny dare fulfilled.
Around the empty plate, three bright jammy pawprints made a wobbly circle. Nia grinned at the surprising taste, Ada laughed, and Pip saluted his label with a crumb stuck to his nose.
The shared button became crumbs, and the label hung from the stall while those crumbs made a little cinnamon constellation. Ada, Nia, and Pip stood beneath it, each with a berry-bright smile.
The label dangled from the stall, swinging above a constellation of crumbs. Ada had one crumb on her nose, Nia had jam on her thumb, and Pip claimed the brightest crumb as his personal star.
